summary: apigw send-window saturation delaying TTFB during KV cache warmup for long-completions
description: Issue summary: Customers are observing large spikes in time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for streaming long-completions during KV cache warmup. Impact: Increased latency (TTFB 3–20s) causes UI timeouts and several customer retries. Behavior is intermittent and correlates with long prompt streams and large tracing headers. Environment: Production (us-east), Dedicated cluster for LexiDocs; traffic routed through api-gateway -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime. Expected: TTFB consistently < 500ms for first token on warmed GPU. Observed: First token delayed between 3s and 20s; subsequent tokens stream normally once first chunk goes through.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a long prompt or a generation with kv-cache warmup (e.g., 2k token context + long system prompt).
2) Send request via customer client that attaches tracing headers (~>8KB) and a large auth cookie (3–4KB).
3) Observe request passing through customer LB -> Redwood API Gateway -> edge-proxy -> serving runtime.
4) Note TTFB delay before first chunk arrives; stream resumes normally afterwards.
Curl reproduction example: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Trace: <large-baggage>' -d '{"input":"<long-prompt>"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
logs: edge-proxy access: request_id=req_2f9b, total_request_size_headers=13KB, backend_connect=20ms, first_byte_to_backend=3100ms, first_byte_to_client=3205ms
apigw metric: upstream_send_window_saturated=42 (count in 1h window), stalled_writes=7
serving-runtime logs: kv-cache: warmup_start ts=2026-01-19T14:12:04Z, first_token_emitted ts=2026-01-19T14:12:08Z (4s gap), worker-gpu-7 utilization spike during warmup
ALB logs: TargetResponseTime spike at 2026-01-19T14:12:xxZ for target arn:aws:.../i-08xx (3.9s)
Sample trace link: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/2f9b-xyz (span: edge-proxy->upstream write wait 3.1s)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Large headers + client chunking cause edge-proxy to buffer and coalesce writes; upstream socket send buffer gets saturated while runtime is busy with KV warmup leading to stalled writes and delayed first byte.
Confirmed that incidents cluster when kv-cache miss rates are high (new sessions) and requests carry large baggage headers (>10KB combined).

Edge-proxy config: send_buffer_threshold default 16KB; observed multiple flush cycles where proxy refrained from flush until buffer threshold reached or backend signaled writable. This increases latency when backend CPU/GPU busy during warmup.

Reproduced locally by toggling 'edge-proxy:coalesce_writes=on' and simulating 2s synthetic KV warmup: enabling coalescing reproduces TTFB spike, disabling coalescing removes spike but increases small-chunk overhead.
APIGW/ALB idle timeouts do not directly reset streams here; it's a server-side write stall rather than mid-stream reset.
comments: Support (Maya Patel) 2026-01-19: Customer reported UI flickers and multiple 'request timed out' errors. Provided initial packet captures and asked for SRE triage. (Slack: #support @lexidocs)

SRE (Ravi Singh) 2026-01-19: Collected traces and identified upstream write-wait spans ~3s on first-token. Marked suspected area: edge-proxy write coalescing + send-window behaviour. Assigned to edge-proxy team for config analysis.

Edge-proxy eng (Ana Torres) 2026-01-20: Reproduced locally; pushed test patch toggling coalescing config. Observed TTFB reduction from median 4.1s -> 0.45s for reproduction workload. Creating PR to add runtime tunable. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/742)

Customer (LexiDocs - PM Oliver Chen) 2026-01-20: Confirmed impact on their session creation flows; requested a workaround pin until patch rolls out to dedicated cluster. Asked about potential cost/regressions for turning coalescing off.

Support (Maya Patel) 2026-01-21: Provided temporary mitigation steps: 1) Reduce client header baggage; 2) Avoid sending large cookies on initial warmup requests; 3) Toggle per-route 'coalesce_writes=false' in dedicated config (documented).
resolution: Workaround applied: per-route config 'coalesce_writes=false' deployed to LexiDocs dedicated ingress on 2026-01-21 (rollout id: r-3312). PR #742 merged to edge-proxy to expose smaller default buffer and runtime toggle. Full rollout to prod clusters scheduled 2026-01-25 with gradual canary; monitoring dashboards show TTFB back within SLO for affected customer after workaround. Follow-ups: 1) Add automated alert when upstream_send_window_saturated > 10/min; 2) Update docs with guidance on header size and auth cookie best practices; 3) Consider adaptive coalescing that disables during KV warmup windows.
